issues.title: review comments from Carl W
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
From: Carl Wallace 
Subject: [Rats] Review of draft-novak-rats-tacra-01
Archived-At: 
 <https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/rats/D7Z6QKWcz86n0STfF9AacUCKVMA>

I have reviewed both draft-novak-rats-tacra-01 and (briefly) draft-novak-lamps-tacra-est. I think TACRA seems like a good avenue to explore but the current draft buries the lede. Some comments on draft-novak-rats-tacra-01 are below.

```

See also https://github.com/TheBankster/rats-tacra/issues/2

issues.title: should attester present a PKCS10 object?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body: 6) Re: design goal 4, draft-novak-lamps-tacra-est has the attester presenting a PKCS #10 object, so it is not clear to me where this transparency line is being drawn (or if it is achievable). The transparency notion is muddied by the inclusion of the CAAPI client inside the attester and the fact that generating a CSR requires inputs that are not part of the proposed API, i.e., credential type would not have subject name.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: The profile already puts names under the Credential Authority's policy ("MUST NOT mint identities (e.g., DNS names) beyond policy for the attested identity context"), and TACRA's Credential Hint section makes the hint a request, not an authorization. What may help is to say what the CSR is for here: proof of possession of CSKpri, not a statement of names. The Attester then needs no subject name: the reference CA takes the name from the Credential Hint or the CSR's common name and refuses anything outside policy ([est_server.py#L82-L84](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/est_server.py#L82-L84)). Suggest one sentence to that effect in the Enrollment section.

issues.title: where does key generation occur?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
10) Re: design goals in general, should there be a design goal focused explicitly on when/where key generation occurs, i.e., freshly generated by attester, freshly generated by CAS, factory generated, already held by the Secret Vault, etc.?  Should there be any goals related to attester identity (and attester authentication to the CAS in general)?
```

(I think this is EST related)

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: TACRA already places key generation in the Credential Acquisition Interface, inside the Attester (Architecture Meeting Design Goals: the CAI generates the CSK for Enrollment and the CEK for Retrieval); in the reference implementation both are fresh for each acquisition ([attester.py#L143](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/attester.py#L143), [attester.py#L164](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/attester.py#L164)). What the drafts do not say is that factory-provisioned keys and keys already held by a Secret Vault are out of scope; one sentence would settle Carl's list. On Attester authentication to the CAS: it is not needed for security, since the CAS is untrusted and the Attester's identity comes from its Evidence (TACRA, CAS Client Authentication to CAS Server). Leaving open for the out-of-scope sentence.

issues.title: secrets encrypted to CEKpub
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
11) Section 4.4 states "resulting secrets are encrypted to CEKpub, ensuring that only the Attester in possession of CEKpri can decrypt them". How does the secret vault establish that it should release a secret to CEKpub?
```

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: Two checks. The binding shows that CEKpub belongs to the attested environment: CEKpub is an input of the digest the Evidence carries, and the Secret Vault recomputes it with the CEKpub of the request before releasing anything ([est_server.py#L115](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/est_server.py#L115); rats-tacra PR #1, Binding Credential Keys to Evidence). The Vault's policy on the Attestation Results then decides which secret that environment may have ([est_server.py#L111](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/est_server.py#L111)). Ready to close once the binding PR is merged.

issues.title: How can EST/RFC7030 be used with AR?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
12) Re: design goal 6, how can the API be used to support passport mode given it has no representation of Attestation Results? 
```

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: Already covered by the text. In the Passport model the CAS Server takes the Evidence to the Verifier and forwards the Attestation Results to the Credential Authority or Secret Vault (TACRA, Architecture Meeting Design Goals; this profile, step 7 of the Enrollment and Retrieval figures). The Attester never handles Attestation Results, which is how design goal 6 keeps the two models indistinguishable to it, so the API needs no representation of them. Closing; reopen if the text should say this more plainly.

issues.title: How is trust established in CAS?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
13) In general, the draft would benefit from describing how trust moves in the architecture, i.e., how do the attester, Secret Vault, and Credential Authority establish trust in the CAS, how do the Secret Vault and Credential Authority trust the Verifier, etc.
```

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: Same question as TheBankster/rats-tacra#11. TACRA's section "Credential Acquisition System Considered Untrustworthy" already treats the CAS as untrusted, and the Trust Model PR will set out who trusts whom. Closing as a duplicate of rats-tacra#11, where the discussion continues.

issues.title: how should initial credential types be handled
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
14) Would the API benefit from only passing credential type to the initiation interface (to avoid calling enroll for one credential type with a handle initialized for a different credential type)? Similarly, should there be a List-Supported-Credential-Types interface?
```

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: The first half is how the reference server already behaves: an Enrollment or Retrieval whose Target or credential type differs from its initiate is refused (403 initiation-mismatch, [est_server.py#L350](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/est_server.py#L350)). Whether credential_type goes on the wire at all is still open; Mark noted in the review of PR #1 that fewer on-the-wire parameters are better. A List-Supported-Credential-Types call could be the CAS Client's local knowledge rather than a wire operation.

issues.title: is Proof-of-Possession only way?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```

15) In section 2, Credential Enrollment is defined only in terms of proof-of-possession credentials. That leaves no mode for a newly minted bearer token, e.g., a JWT issued on demand. Section 2 lists JWTs and API keys as Bearer Token Credentials and design goal 2 commits to supporting them. The API precludes them as Enroll-Credential requires a CSR and Retrieve-Credential is defined as fetching a pre-existing credential. Is it necessarily the case that only proof-of-possession credentials would require enrollment (especially given future proofing goals)?
```

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: TACRA already supports bearer tokens while discouraging them (Undesirability and Inevitability of Bearer Tokens), and delivers them sealed to CEKpub. A token minted on demand needs no new leg: the Relying Party mints it at release time and seals it to CEKpub with origin authentication, as a stored secret is released ([est_server.py#L115](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/est_server.py#L115)). So Enrollment can stay proof-of-possession with a CSR, and the definition of Retrieval can say "existing or newly minted".

Rows 1 to 19 describe the commits as they were made; where commit 20 changed their result (`server_id` is now `rrp_id`, the absent-timestamp `handle` is back), row 20 says so. Each commit message says what was hard to turn into an edit and how the text resolves it. Where a decision is the authors' to make, the alternative is stated here rather than in the draft. The commits are kept apart so that each item can be reviewed on its own; they can be squashed on merge.

Corrections to my 22 September note, found while checking every claim: the csr-attestation attribute is `id-aa-attestation` in -29, not `id-aa-evidence`; and the 300 s nonce lifetime I mentioned, which I first dropped because I could not re-verify it, is now verified in the SIG implementation's source (`internal/mockca/attest.go`, `nonceLifetime`) and cited in 8.1.1.

The hardware run behind the appendices, in one paragraph. Google Cloud `n2d-standard-2` (EPYC Milan, SEV firmware 1.58 build 1, SEV-SNP active), code at `tacra-est` e116768fe989, run 20260926T234654Z. The Attester makes no network request: it takes the VCEK, ASK and ARK from the host's certificate table. The report is VCEK-signed; its signature and the VCEK → ASK → ARK chain verify with OpenSSL, and the pinned ARK is DER-identical to the ARK-Milan that AMD's KDS serves. REPORT_DATA equals the SHA-512 digest of the binding input (Handle, `rrp_id`, Target, CSR; 320 octets), recomputed independently from the test vector. All 23 drills behave as on the mock: honest enrollment and retrieval in all five Freshness Kinds, including `attest-initiate` completed locally; a moved epoch answered 409 and the retry issued; a timestamp older than `max_age` answered 409; RRP substitution and Target substitution refused with `binding-mismatch` under this text and issued under -00; with the RRP identifier taken from the response instead of held, the conduit's choice of RRP issues (D3b), as the ProVerif model predicts; one `absent-timestamp` request refused at a second RRP under this text and issued by both CAs under -00; bundle substitution refused by the Attester under this text and accepted under -00; a replayed Handle answered 409. D10's report met the host's throttle and took 10.2 s, the wait the Handle Lifetime floor is for. Verifier time on the server 31.1 ms median; the enrollment request is 17 395 bytes with the certificate chain inside the Evidence. All seven messages validate against the CDDL, and the three negative controls are refused.

The draft builds with the repository's Makefile (kramdown-rfc 1.7.43, xml2rfc 3.34.1); the two "both inline and in YAML header" notes for RFC 7030 and RFC 9334 pre-date this PR.

Artifact: `nikolaichuk7/tacra-est` holds the twenty-four ProVerif models with their output, the reference implementation (Attester, honest and dishonest conduits, EST Server with the three resources and all five Freshness Kinds, Verifier for SEV-SNP and a mock, CA, Vault with HPKE `mode_auth`), the drills, the CDDL check, and the raw evidence of every run with the SHA-256 sums taken on the VM.

## Interop with the TWI SIG implementation

The SIG's own EST fork (`TWI-Unified-Model/globalsign-est`) is a second, independent implementation. Both carry the Target and the Credential Type as the `target` and `credential_type` query parameters of `attest-initiate`, and both choose the mode, enrollment or retrieval, by a per-Target policy. Running our findings against it, through its public Go API, confirms both cases in its own code (`tacra-est/interop/`, `RESULTS.txt`):

- The `csr-hash` binding is declared and its presence required, but `CSRHash()` is never called on the verify path and the mock EAT omits the CSR, so a swapped CSR is issued a certificate (key substitution).
- `SealCredentialBundle` needs only CEKpub and `Open` does not check the sender, so a bundle sealed by no Vault is accepted (bundle substitution).

Both are the expected state of a declared POC — its own comment names HPKE as "the baseline the specification will ultimately mandate" — and the tests turn that into a reproducing case. This is contributed as interop, not as a vulnerability report.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body:
Pushed fa4cd72, which applies this review in one commit (so the threads above now show as outdated). By thread:

- `server_id` / Evidence produced for an EST Server: it is now `rrp_id`, the RRP that relies on the Evidence (the CA for Enrollment, the Vault for Retrieval); item 4 is Evidence-to-RRP, and the Attester no longer compares identifiers. Which source is required, held or taken from the response, is a TODO in 8.1 for Tuesday.
- absent-timestamp: your rule is back. The timestamp travels in `handle` as 8 octets, seconds since 1970, and the binding input takes it.
- Where the bindings are specified, and exclusive or additive: `evidence` points to the binding input (9.1.5); the five requirements apply together; `binding-input` is the one method, and the other three are only in addition.
- Options: csr-attestation is an optional path, HPKE `mode_auth` is the one mandatory container, and a new 8.1.1 says what is advertised and what is agreed out of band.
- The Retrieval sentence is scoped to Enrollment; Handle Lifetime keeps the requirement and one line of why.
- Left for you: `credential_type` on the wire, and the `acceptable_evidence` / `profile` names.

Also fixed in passing: Implementation Status said the interop with the SIG's code reproduced server substitution; what it reproduced was key substitution and bundle substitution.

The reference implementation now runs all five Freshness Kinds. It was re-run on SEV-SNP (run 20260926T234654Z): all 23 drills behaved as expected, and the appendices are regenerated from that run ([RESULTS](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/docs/RESULTS.md)). The ProVerif set is now 24 models, adding Verifier-issued Handles and the absent-timestamp case ([formal/README.md](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/formal/README.md)). TheBankster/rats-tacra#1 carries the same change to the binding text.

This is not strictly correct; "target" might be a parameter, but Credential Type is (currently) not. It's left to retrieve/enroll phases. This is illustrated here: https://github.com/TWI-Unified-Model/tacra/blob/main/proto/initiate.mmd
It is of course possible that this is a mistake, which then needs to be corrected in the TACRA PoC as well.

The expanded capabilities are noteworthy and likely useful, but they also introduce complexity and a need to either negotiate things or configure them out of band. We should discuss and document what needs to happen.

Thanks, Mark — fast turnaround, appreciated.

I put `credential_type` on `attest-initiate` because two of the sources I was working from carry it there: Section 5.1 of the TACRA draft lists "Credential Type" as an Initiate-Credential-Acquisition parameter and says Initiate validates that the Target, Credential Type and Hint are supported by the CAS; and the TWI reference server sends it on initiate (`attestCredentialTypeParam` in `attest_client.go`). So the profile followed those.

`initiate.mmd` is in a repo I can't open, so I'll defer to it. If the intended model is that only `target` is on the first call and Credential Type is settled in the enroll/retrieve phase, I'll make `credential_type` second-leg only: drop it from the `attest-initiate` query and from the "must equal the initiate" check, keeping the Target match. The binding input never included Credential Type, so nothing else changes. As you note, TACRA Section 5.1 and the PoC's initiate call would then want the same tweak.

Either way is a small edit; tell me which and I'll align the draft and the reference implementation.

Agreed — useful, and it does add complexity. Part of the negotiation surface is already in the profile: the `attest-initiate` response carries `acceptable_evidence` and `acceptable_csk` / `acceptable_cek`, and the `binding` object names the Evidence-to-CSR method, so a server can advertise what it accepts and the client can pick. What isn't written yet is the configuration/policy side: whether a Credential Authority requires csr-attestation inside the CSR in addition to the Evidence beside it, and how that requirement is signalled. I can add a short "negotiation and configuration" note — here and in 9.1.3 — stating what the initiate response advertises and what has to be agreed out of band. Good topic for Tuesday; I'll draft the text whichever way you want it to land.
I would rephrase it. Evidence requirements for Enroll vs. Retrieve are entirely separate, so this sentence reads weird.

My instinct is to specify something rather than leave too much to the implementer, so long as doing so doesn't lock anything major out. We can always add (necessary) complexity later. Too many options at once without at least some validation that each one is actually necessary is a dangerous path to take.

Agreed — that sentence mixes the two modes. This paragraph is about Enrollment's choice between Evidence in the CSR and beside it; Retrieval has no CSR and its Evidence carries CEKpub by construction (Section 9.2.2), which is a separate matter and doesn't belong in the same breath.

I'll drop the trailing sentence and, if it reads better, scope the paragraph explicitly to Enrollment — e.g. after "...a Credential Authority MAY require either or both": "This choice is specific to Enrollment; Retrieval has no CSR and binds Evidence to CEKpub (Section 9.2.2)."

I'll fold this into the revision together with the other two points rather than push it mid-review, so you get one clean update.
This is nowhere in TACRA. Should this be added there?

Agreed, and I'd rather cut than caveat. Concretely, on what's optional here and where it came from:

- The three Evidence-to-CSR methods (CSR Hash, Public Key Thumbprint, Key Certification) are inherited from the base draft's "at least one of". I'd make `binding-input` the single MUST — it is the one specified end to end and validated on hardware — and drop or demote the other two.
- The csr-attestation "either or both" is mine. I'll reduce it to: this profile carries Evidence beside the CSR, and placing attestations in the CSR per csr-attestation is an optional interop path, not a co-equal requirement.
- For the bundle, one mandatory container (HPKE `mode_auth`) instead of the CMS / COSE menu, with the others listed as optional.

That leaves one specified way through Enrollment and one through Retrieval, everything else explicitly optional. Tell me if that's the line you want and I'll write it that way — good to lock on Tuesday.

Good catch — and yes, it belongs in TACRA. PR #1 there (branch binding-to-evidence) already adds it: the freshness input binds four values — the Freshness Handle, "an identifier of the credential-acquisition service that the CAI is configured to use for the Target, such as the origin of an EST Server's URI", the Target, and the CSR or CEKpub. `server_id` in this profile is the EST spelling of that generic service-identifier element, so the two drafts are consistent by construction.

If the TACRA PR wording doesn't make it obvious that `server_id` here is the same element, I'll tighten it there so the mapping is explicit.

This may very well be a security requirement, but currently TACRA does not imbue the Attester with any knowledge of what the Server ID is. In fact, CAS is intended to be fully transparent to the Attester, client and server both. RRP (RATS Relying Party) and Verifier need not be, but we should still talk about what Attester needs to enforce as far as who it generates Evidence for. This should be discussed next Tuesday.

Agreed — that sentence asks the Attester to know something TACRA deliberately keeps from it, and it turns out not to be needed.

I checked before answering. I re-ran the model with the Attester-side comparison removed ([formal/enrollment-bind-nocompare.pv](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/formal/enrollment-bind-nocompare.pv)): the Attester no longer looks at the `server_id` it receives through the CAS; it binds the server identity it holds, and every server recomputes the binding with its own. All three enrollment queries still hold ([results](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/formal/results/proverif-20260926T224122Z.txt)). So the comparison was defence in depth, not what carries the guarantee, and I'll drop the "Attester MUST compare `server_id`" sentence.

What remains, and I agree it's for Tuesday: the value that gets bound has to come from inside the Attester's trust boundary, not from the CAS. TACRA already has the CAI select the mechanism per Target (Design Goal 5), so the CAI's per-Target configuration is the natural source. If the intent is that even that stays out of the Attester's view, then server substitution is prevented only where that identity is configured, and the text should say so. I'll bring both options.
Does this level of detail belong in an IETF I-D? Should we find another home for it? I don't want to lose it, and I don't think its place is here.

Fair — I'd move it. The draft only needs the requirement and one line of why; the platform specifics (the GHCB rate-limit recommendation, the Linux driver's retry constants, the Google Cloud timings) are evidence, not protocol.

Proposed text for this subsection:

> Producing hardware Evidence can be delayed: a platform may rate-limit attestation requests, so an Attester can wait several seconds for the report that carries the Handle. A Handle originator SHOULD NOT set `expires_in` below 60 s; the measurements that motivate the value are in {{TACRA-EST-IMPL}}.

The full detail already lives in the tacra-est repo ([docs/RESULTS.md](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/docs/RESULTS.md), section 4, every source cited), so nothing is lost; the draft just points there. If you'd rather it sit somewhere the WG maintains — the RATS wiki that came up at the interim, or the TWI repo — I can write it up for either.
If credential_type ends up not carried one the wire, as I suspect it won't, then this will need to be reworded.
I thought for absent-timestamp, the handle is the attester's timestamp. Is that not so?
Where are these bindings specified so the implementer knows what do implement?

Understood, and I expect the same. For the record, your original text had it OPTIONAL in the retrieval request only; I made it REQUIRED in both requests to mirror TACRA Sections 5.2-5.3.

If Credential Type stays a CAAPI parameter (CAI to EST Client) and isn't carried in EST, the rewording is contained:

- remove `credential_type` from both request bodies, from `request-common` in the CDDL and from the examples, together with the "MUST equal the preceding `attest-initiate`" clauses; `target` and its match stay;
- add one sentence: the EST Server determines what to mint or release from the Target and its own policy, and the Attester side checks that what comes back is the Credential Type it asked for (for Retrieval that is the CAI after unwrapping, since the CAS never sees inside the bundle).

Two things follow from it, worth settling in the same decision:

1. TACRA Sections 5.1-5.3 list an Unsupported (5.3: Invalid) Credential Type failure. With no type on the wire, the EST Server can't detect it; the CAS Client can, from its own configuration. One sentence in TACRA saying which side checks would keep the two documents consistent.
2. In the TWI globalsign-est fork, the mock CA's `TargetPolicy` allows a list of Credential Types per Target, and its check runs only when a request carries a type (the field is already optional in all three messages there). With nothing on the wire, a Target that allows two types in the same mode, e.g. JWT and API key, both by retrieval, has no way to say which. The simplest rule is one Credential Type per Target and mode, fixed by CAS policy.

I'll fold this into the same revision as your first comment.
Should "acceptable_evidence" then be renamed to "acceptable_profiles"? Otherwise it's not intuitive that one corresponds to the other. Maybe then this can be renamed into "chosen_profile".
Noting something you're like to fix already: Evidence is never produced for an EST Server, only for a Verifier or RRP.
Are these mutually exclusive or additive?

You're right, and my edit broke it. I made `handle` absent for absent-timestamp on the reasoning that the timestamp is a claim inside Evidence, like an EAT `iat`. On a direct-form platform that doesn't hold: an SEV-SNP report has no time field, and REPORT_DATA is the only value the guest chooses, so a timestamp that isn't in the binding input isn't covered by the report's signature at all. absent-timestamp would then give no freshness on exactly the platform we measured. Our implementation exercises present-nonce only, which is why no run caught it.

So I'll restore your rule: `handle` REQUIRED unless `absent-none`, carrying the Attester's timestamp for absent-timestamp, and the binding input takes it like any other freshness element. One detail to fix for interop, since the Relying Party recomputes the binding input byte for byte: the timestamp's encoding. I'd propose an 8-octet big-endian unsigned count of seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z (the NumericDate of JWT and CWT), which the Verifier compares against `max_age`.

In this draft: "Key Binding and PoP Requirements" (`{{key-binding}}` is its anchor) says what must be bound, and "Binding Input" right after it gives the construction: the octet string, its SHA-512 digest in the 64-octet report field, and how the Credential Authority or Secret Vault recomputes it. The appendix "Test Vector for the Binding Input" works one through end to end, and Retrieval reuses the construction with CEKpub as the subject ("Evidence-to-CEK Binding").

Your question does expose a gap, though. An implementer reading the requirements meets three Evidence-to-CSR methods (CSR Hash, Public Key Thumbprint, Key Certification) and a `binding.method` field, and nothing there says that `binding-input` is the method that meets the requirements in one go; the Binding Input section is also scoped to the direct platform form only. For the revision, in line with the options thread: `evidence` MUST carry the binding input, which becomes the single mandatory method; the Binding Input section says where the digest goes in each platform form (the report field itself, or the report data of the nested attestation); and the other methods become optional or go.

Yes, they should read as a pair. Both names are the ones the TWI globalsign-est fork uses, where the value is a media type with an EAT profile parameter (`application/eat+cwt; eat_profile="..."`); in the reference implementation it's a URN naming the SEV-SNP JSON format. Since in LAMPS "profile" tends to read as a certificate profile, and not every value is an EAT profile, I'd lean to `acceptable_evidence_types` / `evidence_type`. `acceptable_profiles` / `chosen_profile` works too. Your call; the fork would change with it.

Agreed. The party that recomputes that binding is already the RRP (the Credential Authority for Enrollment, the Secret Vault for Retrieval), so the fix is naming, not mechanism: `server_id` becomes an RRP identifier, item 4 becomes "Evidence-to-RRP: ... so that Evidence produced for one RRP cannot be presented to another", and the server-substitution item in Security Considerations follows. The EST Server then drops out of the binding entirely.

Where the Attester gets that identifier stays the Tuesday question from your `server_id` comment. One thing to bring to it: if the CAI holds it in per-Target configuration, the Attester knows who it produces Evidence for, but a CAS that moves a Target from enrollment to retrieval (Goal 1) then also has to update the Attester's configuration. If it comes in the `attest-initiate` response instead, the CAS chooses the RRP as it chooses the mode, and the binding would guarantee only that one RRP, and no other, can use the Evidence. I'll have that second case modelled in ProVerif by Tuesday, so both options come with results.

Additive: every request has to meet all five numbered requirements. What reads as alternatives is the list of three Evidence-to-CSR mechanisms under them ("at least one"), and those are only ways to meet item 2. With the binding input as the single mandatory method (see the thread on the `evidence` field), the section becomes all five requirements met by two checks: the CSR signature for item 1, and the binding input for items 2 to 5 (CSR, freshness, RRP, Target) in one digest. I'll make the text say "all of the following".

Modelled now rather than Tuesday: six more variants in the same generator, with the nine earlier models unchanged. Write-up: [formal/README.md](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/formal/README.md#where-the-bound-identity-comes-from-six-more-models); ProVerif output: [results](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/main/formal/results/proverif-20260926T232411Z-rrp-source.txt).

| freshness | identity the Attester binds | the intended RRP issues (Q1) | only the RRP it bound issues (B1) | at most one RRP per CSR and Target (U1) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh Handle per RRP | none | false | | true |
| fresh Handle per RRP | from `attest-initiate` | false | true | true |
| fresh Handle per RRP | from CAI configuration | true | | true |
| shared epoch | none | false | | false |
| shared epoch | from `attest-initiate` | false | true | true |
| shared epoch | from CAI configuration | true | | true |

In short: an identifier that comes through the CAS keeps any one Evidence to one RRP. That matters when freshness isn't per-RRP (the shared-epoch rows); with a per-RRP Handle, the Handle already does it. Only a configured identifier makes it the RRP the deployment intended. And with a local `attest-initiate` there is no response to take the identifier from, so configuration is the only source there.

reviews.author: TheBankster
reviews.body: Excellent content; much of this change belongs in the base TACRA draft.

comments.body: we should consolidate implementation efforts, ideally under the https://github.com/TWI-Unified-Model organization; I invited you.

I think that sending credential type to CAS is proper, but it allows the CAS client to reject credential types that CAS does not support, and client should know that. But that does not mean that it goes on the wire to CAS server. Now, if CAS client is really dumb, or if the credential type depends on what the CAS server thinks based on the Target, then the outcome would be different. I think overall fewer on-the-wire parameters are a good thing as that makes thinks simpler.
BTW same considerations apply to Credential Hint

Identifier of the RRP that would rely on the Evidence is new to me. Let's discuss whether it's appropriate to include it. If the initiate call to the server is never made (if the CAS client short-circuits it), that information would not be available to the CAS client anyways.
Same comment as above on the identifier of the RRP.
TACRA draft currently also allows the inclusion of Credential Hint in "initiate" leg under CAAPI. Unclear if it should be carried on the wire though.
Reference to CDDL (https://www.iana.org/assignments/cddl perhaps?) should be included, no?
Want to discuss: how do we express "acceptable evidence"?
If this is needed, we need to update the TACRA draft accordingly.

Want to discuss: what if the two are missing, and what if they are both present but different?
Also want to discuss: how much of this needs to go into the TACRA draft and simply inherited by all CAS implementations?
This definitely belongs in the base TACRA draft, don't you think?
Grammar error? "unless freshness_kind is absent-none, and absent then:"... I can't parse it.
This reads like a complicated run-on sentence. Break it up for clarity?
The Verifier and the RRP both? Or whoever happens to be checking it?
How is Evidence bound to Target? Is the mechanism worth specifying?
How does Verifier attest to the binding?
This, once again, seems like something that needs to go into the base TACRA draft. I cannot imagine this is EST specific.
I'd capitalize "Direct"
Same: capitalize "Provider-scoped"
Same comment on grammar as above
Is it strictly the same even there is no CSR but in this case there's a CEK?

The authentication trust configuration must be provided out of band then?
(and again, this seems TACRA, not EST, specific)
This needs to go into the base TACRA draft
CAS MUST be outside the Attester's trust boundary; it's not a SHOULD as CAS is not attested as part of Attester.
All of this is amazing content, and most if not all of it belongs in the base TACRA draft, and should be referenced from here.
The link should resolve to the joint implementation. TACRA is currently a private repository. We could open it up when we publish the I-D.

reviews.body: Thanks for the review, and sorry these sat for a week. Eight are done in d637c23, six are already in TACRA, seven are for TheBankster/rats-tacra#17 and TheBankster/rats-tacra#19 on Tuesday, and four come with a proposal. What I say was checked, I ran today on live GCP SEV-SNP and TDX.

comments.body: Done in d637c23: TACRA-EST-IMPL now points to TWI-Unified-Model/tacra, which has the SEV-SNP and TDX back-ends since TWI-Unified-Model/tacra#8. The measurements and models the text cites stay in tacra-est. Should those move under TWI-Unified-Model too, so the draft points to one place?
Agreed, neither has to. That's TheBankster/rats-tacra#19; I'll hold the text until Tuesday.
TACRA now has the CAI hold the RRP identifier (Binding Credential Keys to Evidence, item 3), so it needn't be on the wire. The alternatives are in TheBankster/rats-tacra#17.
Same: TACRA has the CAI hold it (Binding Credential Keys to Evidence, item 3).
Agreed, it can stay out of attest-initiate; with TheBankster/rats-tacra#19.
Done in d637c23 (RFC 8610).

How about media types with parameters, the way Veraison picks its schemes? Each scheme lists the Evidence it takes, e.g. `application/vnd.veraison.tsm-report+cbor` for SEV-SNP and TDX, which is what TWI-Unified-Model/tacra#8 sends. `acceptable_evidence` would be that list, agreed out of band per Target; it also fits the advertised-vs-agreed text you want in TACRA.
TACRA says it now (Binding Credential Keys to Evidence, item 3): the CAI holds the identifier.

Proposed rule: the identifier configured in the CAI is the one bound, and with none configured the Attester refuses. If the CAS takes the request to another RRP, that RRP refuses, because the binding names the configured one. If the identifier comes from the attest-initiate response instead, the CAS gets to choose the RRP; with a set of acceptable identifiers, only within the set. All of these checked today on SEV-SNP and TDX.
Agreed; I'll move it into a TACRA PR, together with the media-type proposal for acceptable_evidence.
Done in d637c23: one line per Freshness Kind.

It's in TACRA now (Binding Credential Keys to Evidence): the Verifier reports the report-data value in the Attestation Results, and the CA or Vault recomputes the digest and rejects a mismatch. Checked today on SEV-SNP and TDX, in Passport and Background Check.
In TACRA now: the Target is part of the binding input. On SEV-SNP and TDX today a target substitution is refused; under -00 it went through.
In the same TACRA section (Binding Credential Keys to Evidence): the Verifier reports the value it read, and the RRP compares it with its own digest.
Done: it's TACRA's Binding Credential Keys to Evidence (TheBankster/rats-tacra#1).
Done in d637c23.
Done in d637c23.
Done in d637c23, the same edit as in the enrollment request.
Yes: the subject is the CSR for Enrollment and CEKpub for Retrieval, and TACRA says so now. The test vector is an Enrollment; the example exchange has a Retrieval from a live SEV-SNP run.

Yes, out of band, per Target in the CAI, like the RRP identifier. One thing to decide first: HPKE-bis (draft-ietf-hpke-hpke-05) removes mode_auth, and the post-quantum KEMs (draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05) can't do it at all. So I'd propose base mode with the Vault signing the sealed bundle, under the same out-of-band key. It runs on SEV-SNP and TDX today with MLKEM768-P256: an unsigned bundle, or one signed by the conduit, is refused. OK to change the container in this PR?
In TACRA now: Binding Credential Keys to Evidence says each value closes a substitution, the RRP identifier included.

Done in d637c23: MUST. That rules out the Attester being the EST Client itself, so I removed that sentence. TACRA still says SHOULD in Summary of RATS Roles, and "leaves open … no trust boundary" in Credential Acquisition System Considered Untrustworthy; want a PR for those?
Agreed. I owe a Trust Model PR for TACRA (I said so in TheBankster/rats-tacra#11); this goes there, and the EST text will point to it.
